\title{Exact Haar Entropy in the Local $SU(2)$ Partition Comparison}
\author{}
\date{21 July 2026}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We isolate the exact geometric entropy paid by small comparison sets in
$SU(2)$.  The result removes an ambiguity in the conditional partition-ratio
frontier: a local denominator ball has cubic, rather than Gaussian, Haar mass,
and its negative logarithm must be paid by the available action gap.  The
statement is finite-dimensional and exact; it does not bound the complete
Yang--Mills numerator.
\end{abstract}

Equip $SU(2)\cong S^3$ with its bi-invariant geodesic metric and normalized
Haar probability $\mu_H$.  Write $B_r(g)=\{h:d(g,h)\le r\}$ and
$v(r)=\mu_H(B_r(g))$, which is independent of $g$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact ball and shell mass]
For $0\le r\le\pi$,
\[
 v(r)=\frac{r-\sin r\cos r}{\pi}
     =\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^r\sin^2u\,du,
 \qquad
 v'(r)=\frac{2\sin^2r}{\pi}.
\]
Consequently a shell $a\le d(g,h)\le b$ has normalized mass $v(b)-v(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Geodesic polar coordinates on the unit three-sphere have volume element
$4\pi\sin^2u\,du$, while $\operatorname{vol}(S^3)=2\pi^2$.  Division by the
total volume gives the integral.  Integration and differentiation give the
two displayed formulas.  Bi-invariance removes the center $g$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Certified small-ball entropy]
For $0\le r\le1$,
\[
 \frac{2r^3}{3\pi}\left(1-\frac{r^2}{5}\right)
 \le v(r)\le \frac{2r^3}{3\pi}.
\]
For $0<r\le1$ this is equivalently
\[
 \log\frac{3\pi}{2r^3}
 \le -\log v(r)
 \le \log\frac{3\pi}{2r^3}
       -\log\left(1-\frac{r^2}{5}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On $[0,1]$, $u-u^3/6\le\sin u\le u$.  Hence
$u^2(1-u^2/3)\le\sin^2u\le u^2$; the omitted $u^6/36$ term is nonnegative.
Integration in the exact formula gives the volume bounds.  The logarithm is
order preserving and $-\log$ reverses the volume inequalities as displayed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-center atlas]
The radius-$\pi/2$ balls about $I$ and $-I$ cover $SU(2)$.  Each has Haar mass
$1/2$; their intersection is the equatorial two-sphere and has Haar measure
zero.  The atlas therefore has multiplicity one almost everywhere and two on
the common boundary.
\end{corollary}

\section*{Meaning for the partition-ratio programme}
At the Stage 25 local radius $r=0.00614955590043087$, the exact denominator
entropy $-\log v(r)$ is recorded by the accompanying executable certificate.
The leading behavior is
\[
 -\log v(r)=3\log(1/r)+\log(3\pi/2)+O(r^2).
\]
Thus shrinking a comparison ball improves local Taylor control while charging
three logarithmic entropy units per radial decade.  Any proof based on a
denominator restriction must retain this cost.  A pointwise action minimum,
without its integration volume and boundary-state normalizer, is insufficient.

\begin{remark}[Claim boundary]
The theorem proves Haar geometry only.  It does not compare the nonlinear
good partition uniformly over retained boundary states, estimate the charged
bad numerator, establish volume-uniform basin entry, iterate an RG map, or
construct a continuum Hamiltonian.
\end{remark}
